title: pOdometry Mail Handling

notebook.text:
The pattern you are using is fragile because it mixes data ingestion with logic execution, leading to inaccuracies and inconsistent performance. In the MOOS architecture, applications are designed around a specific split of responsibilities between OnNewMail() and Iterate().
Conceptual Split: OnNewMail() vs. Iterate()
OnNewMail() (The In-Box): Its purpose is to parse the list of incoming messages and update the internal state (member variables) of your application
1
2
. It should be kept as lean as possible. You should not perform "work"—like heavy calculations or publishing results—here because OnNewMail() frequency is tied to the arrival of mail, not the application's internal clock
2
.
Iterate() (The Workroom): This is where the primary work of the application is orchestrated
3
. It runs at a frequency approximately defined by the AppTick parameter in your .moos file
4
. Calculations, logic transitions, and publications (Notify) belong here to ensure they happen at a consistent, predictable rate
5
6
.
Why Your Current Pattern is Fragile
Intermediate Point Loss ("The Gotcha"): Navigation variables like NAV_X are typically published by uSimMarine at 10Hz
7
. If your app runs at a standard 4Hz, you will receive 2–3 messages per iteration
7
. Your current loop overwrites m_x and m_y for every message but only calculates the distance once after the loop. This means you are calculating a straight line between the start of the iteration and the very last point received, effectively "cutting corners" and losing total distance traveled
7
.
Publication Frequency: By calling Notify() inside OnNewMail(), you publish every time mail is handled. If mail arrives in bursts or is delayed, your output variable becomes irregular. Moving Notify() to Iterate() ensures your odometry updates are consistent with your AppTick
7
8
.
Variable Naming: Per the standard lab specifications, the expected MOOS variable is ODOMETRY_DIST, not ODOM_DIST
5
9
.
Corrected Pattern Conceptually
To make this robust, you should capture the updates in the mail loop and perform the math and publication in the iteration loop. To solve the "intermediate point" problem mentioned in the sources, you should update the distance tally inside the mail loop for every navigation update received
7
.
bool Odometry::OnNewMail(MOOSMSG_LIST &NewMail)
{
  AppCastingMOOSApp::OnNewMail(NewMail); // Standard for appcasting [10]

  for(auto msg : NewMail) {
    string key = msg.GetKey();
    if(key == "NAV_X" || key == "NAV_Y") {
      // Update coordinates
      if(key == "NAV_X") m_current_x = msg.GetDouble();
      if(key == "NAV_Y") m_current_y = msg.GetDouble();

      // If this isn't the very first reading, add the delta to the total
      if(!m_first_reading) {
        m_total_dist += hypot(m_current_x - m_previous_x, m_current_y - m_previous_y);
      }
      
      // Update "previous" to the point we just processed
      m_previous_x = m_current_x;
      m_previous_y = m_current_y;
      m_first_reading = false;
    }
  }
  return true;
}

bool Odometry::Iterate()
{
  AppCastingMOOSApp::Iterate(); // Standard bookkeeping [11]

  // Publish the accumulated total at the consistent AppTick frequency
  Notify("ODOMETRY_DIST", m_total_dist);

  AppCastingMOOSApp::PostReport(); // Trigger appcasting [11]
  return true;
}

Diagnostic Checklist for Debugging
Check the .moos file: Ensure AppTick and CommsTick are set correctly (e.g., 4 or 10)
4
8
.
Verify Subscriptions: Ensure your OnStartUp() function or a helper method is actually calling Register("NAV_X", 0) and Register("NAV_Y", 0)
5
10
.
Scope the DB: Use uXMS to see if NAV_X/Y are changing and if ODOMETRY_DIST is being posted
11
12
.
Check for Staleness: If the distance stops updating, check if uSimMarine is still running or if navigation data has gone stale
13
14
.
